D023-D008_h022.question_both: Lately, things have been… a lot. For about a month now, I’ve found myself just devouring food, especially when I’m off the road. I’ll polish off a whole pizza, then grab a bag of chips and a pint of ice cream, all in one sitting. I hate how full I get, like I'm going to burst, but I just can't seem to stop once I start. I try to eat alone, parked up somewhere isolated, because honestly, I’m embarrassed by how much I'm putting away. It’s not just the eating though. I’ve been feeling really revved up, like I don’t need much sleep. I’ll be up all night planning new routes to optimize fuel efficiency, or sketching out designs for a custom sleeper cab. My mind just races, jumping from one idea to the next, and I feel like I could conquer anything. But then, it all just… deflates, and I feel like a truck stuck in the mud.
D023-D008_h022.question_a:
"Well doc, it’s been a rough few months, I guess since my divorce finalized. The biggest thing is this eating. I find myself just devouring huge amounts of food, way more than anyone should. I’ll be on the road, pull over, and just… eat and eat until my stomach hurts, like Thanksgiving dinner every other day. I usually do it alone, parked up somewhere isolated, because honestly, I’m embarrassed by how much I can put away. It’s been happening at least a few times a week, basically since Christmas.

I know what you're probably thinking, especially with how wired I can get sometimes – I’ll have these stretches where I feel invincible, sleep maybe two or three nights a week, and start these huge projects, convinced I can fix everything. But it never lasts, and it’s not like it’s completely throwing my life into chaos or anything. I'm still doing my routes, still managing, you know? It's just this eating thing that really gets to me. It's like I can't stop once I start, and then I just feel awful about myself afterward."
D023-D008_h022.question_b:
"Lately, things have been… a lot. I’m 43, divorced, been driving trucks for years, and usually, I can handle the isolation. But these past few weeks, it's like my mind is racing non-stop. I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours, but I feel wired, full of energy like I could conquer the world. I've been making impulsive decisions, spending money I don’t really have on upgrading my rig, convinced I’m on the verge of some big breakthrough.

Then there’s the eating. I can be driving, and suddenly I just *need* to pull over. I’ll buy bags of chips, giant sodas, candy – whatever I can get my hands on. I eat until my stomach hurts, way past being full, usually in the cab by myself so no one sees how much I'm putting away. It's not just the eating though, it’s everything else too, this intense energy and feeling on top of the world, then crashing hard – it feels like more than just about the food.”
